page: Microsoft Azure E20ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by the AMD EPYC 7763 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, clocking at 3.525 GHz. The instance is configured with 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 10 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. CPU cache includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Cryptographic instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, alongside BMI2, ADX, and AVX, while AVX-512 extensions are absent.

Memory capacity is configured at 160 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio with 8 GB per vCPU. The instance bundles 805 GB of local SSD temporary storage and supports Azure Premium Storage for persistent workloads. There are no discrete hardware accelerators included, with GPU count standing at zero. Benchmark metrics show reliable execution across balanced memory-intensive tasks, delivering 69.4 GB/sec large-block uncached read throughput, 40.77 GB/sec write throughput, and over 20.33 million Redis SET operations per second.

Compute testing demonstrates strong single-core stress-ng performance within the top 25% tier, complemented by an average multi-core stress-ng rating and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,289. While smaller language models run efficiently, generating 317.8 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model, execution bottlenecks emerge on larger 70B parameter models due to the absence of dedicated GPUs. The configuration offers strong resource density for high-RAM enterprise services, making it suited for in-memory caching layers, relational databases, analytics processing, and enterprise application hosting.
description: Microsoft Azure E20ads_v5 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 20 dedicated vCPUs and 160 GB of RAM, derived from an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz across 10 physical cores. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, it features an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside 805 GB of local SSD temporary storage and Premium Storage capability. The instance provides strong single-thread performance alongside solid memory bandwidth, recording 69.4 GB/sec read and 40.77 GB/sec write bandwidth, plus 20.33 million Redis SET operations per second. Lacking hardware accelerators, it is unsuited for massive AI model processing but provides a cost-effective, dense hardware footprint for memory-bound production workloads such as in-memory data grids, relational database engines, and large-scale data processing pipelines.
